observations: Three photos show a large office machine (copier/printer) wrapped tightly in clear plastic film, apparently in a warehouse (wooden pallet visible).
Photo 1 shows a side panel with a partial logo reading 'digital' and a blue energy-star-like sticker, plus visible paper tray labels 'A4' and 'A3'.
A black rectangle (apparent censor box) covers text on the front panel in photo 0 and on the side in photo 1 and 2, obscuring what could be a brand/model plate.
No screen, control panel, power cable, or any powered-on state is visible in any photo.
No visible photo of a nameplate, serial number, or the full 'AR-M207' text seller references.
Watermark 'SMATECH MEGA EQUIPMENT' overlaid on all three photos, consistent with a reseller listing site, not a personal seller photo.

claims.evidence: No nameplate or model text is visible in any photo; black boxes cover the area where such text would be.

claims.claim: 'London use' (implying grade A, lightly used import)
claims.evidence: No usage counter, print sample, or condition detail shown; plastic wrap obscures the body.
Machine is not shown powered on, no test print or display visible in any photo.

risks.risk: Actual model may differ from the claimed AR-M207, affecting toner compatibility, print speed, and price tier.
risks.proof: Clear close-up photo of the model/serial nameplate, unobstructed by plastic wrap or black censor boxes.
risks.if_unproven: priced as a generic unidentified office photocopier, lowest comparable tier

risks.risk: Machine may not power on or may have print quality defects (drum, fuser, toner issues common in used copiers).
risks.proof: Video of unit powered on, producing a test copy or print.

risks.risk: Hidden physical damage (cracks, missing trays, broken glass) concealed by the plastic wrap.
risks.proof: Photos with wrap removed, showing all sides and the scanner glass/lid open.

risks.risk: Page/usage counter unknown, which strongly affects resale value of used copiers.
risks.proof: Photo of the usage counter screen or printed counter report.

risks.risk: Seller's deliberate blacking-out of nameplate/text is unusual and could mask a different, lower-value model being mis-sold as AR-M207.
risks.proof: Unedited, unobstructed photo of the full front and side panels with all original labels visible.
risks.if_unproven: treated as unverified identity, priced at generic lowest tier

proof_requests: Unobstructed close-up photo of the model/serial nameplate (remove plastic wrap and any covering).
Video of the machine powered on, making a test copy/print.
Photo or screenshot of the usage/page counter.
Full-body photos from all four sides and with covers/lids open, wrap removed.
response.reason: The photos deliberately obscure the nameplate/model area with plastic wrap and black boxes, so the seller's AR-M207 claim cannot be confirmed from any photo, and no power-on or usage evidence is shown; a worst-case price cannot be set without knowing whether this is even the claimed model or a lesser unit.
